answers: How many bindings that E508 called module constants are function locals?
58 of the bindings (80 sites, 23 distinct surfaces).
Does any caller hand a real population to those surfaces?
10 of 58 bindings have at least one call site passing a literal container or a module-scope constant; 48 have no such caller.
How many of those surfaces are never called at all in this tree?
0 of 58 bindings have no call site.
Which locals are themselves produced by a call into another module?
11 bindings, into 4 distinct dependency modules; a further 10 are a method call on a value the caller already holds, which is not another module.
Are the call sites mostly omitting the argument?
248 call sites were read: 0 pass a default, 18 a literal, 21 a module constant, 183 a local, 0 a call result.
method_limits: call sites are matched by callee name inside the module that defines the surface (a fallback pass matches the bare name across the tree); a call through an alias of the surface is not seen

an argument that is a name counts as a population only when that name is bound at module scope of the surface's own module; a local is recorded as a local even when the caller's local is itself a module constant
only the first parameter of each binding is used to index call arguments; a binding that reaches two different parameters is counted under the first

a local produced by ``x.method()`` is counted as built by another module only when ``x`` is an import alias of that module; when ``x`` is a value the caller already holds the call is published under its own counter, because a method on a value names no module
whether a caller's expression really covers every branch is not measured here: this face answers who supplies what, not whether the branch is guarded
